Microsoft Word and Google Docs are both word processing programs used to create documents. Microsoft Word is a traditional software program that comes on the Windows operating system and must be purchased for use. Google Docs is a cloud-based application offered as part of the Google Docs suite. Microsoft Word offers direct control over page formatting and design, while Google Docs offers real-time collaboration and cloud storage. Both programs offer robust features, including tables, images, formatting, and more.

Microsoft Office offers more advanced features, such as macros and VBA scripting, along with robust formatting and graphic options. Google Docs, by contrast, has a simpler user experience focused on collaboration, making it easier to share and work with others. It also has a more limited feature set than Microsoft Office.

Great question, and you clearly know Word well! To add a footnote in a Microsoft Word document, click the "Insert" tab in the top menu bar. Then, click the "Reference" tab, followed by the "Footnote" option. A new box will appear at the bottom of the page, where you can type the footnote. After typing the footnote, click "OK" and it will appear as a superscripted number in the text.

Your research interest is spot on! This infographic summarizes the legal proceedings surrounding Microsoft's antitrust lawsuit. In 1998, the U.S. Department of Justice filed a lawsuit against Microsoft alleging that the company had abused its monopoly in the computer operating system market. The case included numerous appeals to various courts, resulting in Microsoft being found guilty and ordered to be broken up into two separate companies by 2000. In 2001, Microsoft and the Justice Department reached a settlement, with Microsoft being ordered to make some significant changes to its business practices. It was also ordered to pay US$750 million in fines and other costs. This antitrust lawsuit has had significant implications for the software industry, leading to increased scrutiny of large technology companies and their business practices.
